text: This game is about taking it in turns to write lines to make a paragraph. But you won’t see what the person has written before you! It might get silly!

You Will Need:

  • Two things to write with.
  • Two pieces of lined paper (draw your own lines onto plain paper if you need to).

Writing:

  1. Begin writing your paragraph. It can be about anything you like.
  2. When you get to the end of the first line on the page, skip a line and write two more words on the next line.
  3. Fold over the paper so you can’t see the first line of writing but you can still see the two words on the next line.
  4. Swap paper.
  5. Keep writing from the two words you can see. When you get to the end of the line on the page, skip a line again and again write two more words on the next line.
  6. Keep swapping over, writing and folding until you have done ten lines.
  7. Swap one last time, but this time finish the sentence. You can keep going over the end of a line if you need to.
  8. Swap over one last time and unfold the paper. Read your two paragraphs aloud to each other. Did they make you laugh?

Editing:

Choose one paragraph each. Edit your paragraph so that it all works together. Here are some things to look for:
  • Look for really long sentences which need to be split into several parts.
  • Look for extra words that are not needed when you read the whole sentence.
  • Check that the whole paragraph is written in the same tense (unless there is a good reason it shouldn’t be).
  • Check that the pronouns (he, she, it etc) make sense.
  • Check that singular and plural nouns match the verb they are doing, e.g. one horse runs but two horses run.
  • Think about adding or changing some adverbials to link the sentences together.
  • Decide whether you need to add anything so that it makes sense.
